main_body: A small wooden bucket about 11px wide and 8px tall. It has a light rim at row 6, a thin dark inner row, a green slop smear and a gray handle across the top, and a brown stave body with iron-gray hoops.
top_band: Only a 1-row light brown rim at row 6 (#b77246), then a dark row 7 (#434326). No multi-row top surface.
evidence: The column at x=8 reads: gray handle at row 4, gap, light rim at row 6, dark row 7, then brown staves and gray hoops down to the outline at row 13. The rim is 1px, and the opening is at most 1-2px with no readable ellipse of the interior. The slop appears as a flat green band on the front rather than a surface seen from above. This matches the guide's 'barrel: lid 2px' and rim-only failures, so there is no real top surface and no visible inside.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 9 distinct colours, against 38-40 in the references. The measured colours-per-tile figure is 0 because the piece is smaller than one tile, so I judged by eye. It is far below the references in colour count, and its material ramps are shallow, with about 3 steps on the wood and one on the hoops. The outline is tinted dark brown (0% neutral edge pixels), which is fine. There is no grain or per-stave texture, and the slop and handle are single flat colours. Next to the cheese stall and the roofed well it looks much thinner and more sticker-like.
